summary:
S.H.I.E.L.D. (Space Health, Intervention, Evaluation & Life Defense) is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring platform developed by team Avengers not Assembled for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

During missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays with Earth can make immediate medical assistance impossible. S.H.I.E.L.D. addresses this challenge by bringing health monitoring, personalized insights, and actionable guidance into one interface that can operate without constant communication with Earth.

Our functional web prototype integrates four key modules: physical health monitoring through an interactive 3D anatomical model, mental health assessment using voice and behavioral indicators, personalized radiation-related nutritional recommendations, and bone and muscle monitoring to support recovery and preparation for returning to gravity.

Unlike conventional monitoring approaches, S.H.I.E.L.D. focuses on each astronaut’s individual health baseline rather than relying solely on general population standards. Its design prioritizes clear visual indicators, discreet vibration alerts, and human-controlled AI recommendations.

Currently demonstrated using simulated data, S.H.I.E.L.D. represents a step toward safer, more autonomous space exploration, empowering astronauts to understand their health and respond to potential risks when Earth is out of reach.
details:
What happens when an astronaut faces a medical emergency millions of kilometers from Earth, with no doctor available and communication delayed by up to 40 minutes?

That is the problem we set out to solve.

S.H.I.E.L.D. (Space Health, Intervention, Evaluation & Life Defense) is an autonomous health monitoring platform designed to give astronauts something essential for deep-space exploration: the ability to understand their health and take informed action without depending on immediate assistance from Earth.

Instead of overwhelming astronauts with disconnected medical readings, S.H.I.E.L.D. brings everything together in one intuitive interface through four interconnected systems:

  • Physical Health: An interactive 3D human body that highlights potential health risks and recommends examinations.
  • Mental Health: Voice, sleep, and behavioral indicators designed to identify stress and fatigue and suggest personalized support.
  • Radiation & Nutrition: Personalized nutritional recommendations based on radiation exposure and inflammatory indicators.
  • Bone & Muscle Health: Monitoring and predictive tools to help astronauts maintain physical condition and prepare for their return to gravity.

What makes S.H.I.E.L.D. different isn't just what it monitors, but how it understands each astronaut.

Rather than relying solely on general medical averages, our system compares health indicators against each individual's personal baseline. Its proposed onboard AI explains changes, prioritizes alerts, and recommends actions while keeping astronauts in control.

We also designed S.H.I.E.L.D. for the realities of space: discreet vibration alerts instead of stressful alarms, an interface understandable without medical training, and local processing that does not require constant contact with Earth.

Our team developed a working web prototype using the BodyParts3D anatomical resource, Python-based anatomical layers, simulated health data, and research from NASA, CSA, and ESA. We also incorporated insights from consultations with an astronaut and a research nutritionist. The interactive 3D model and nutritional planning features are functional with simulated data; advanced analysis, real sensor integration, and clinical validation remain future goals.

Our vision goes beyond monitoring astronauts. We want to make space exploration safer by giving crews greater autonomy when they need it most.
